items.title: What if the framing had matched the sponsor's incentives sooner?
items.description: In the rollback story, Attempt 2 reached a real sponsor (the infra manager, with genuine budget authority) but framed the pitch around the proposal's own correctness — shown here as about 20% aligned with what that manager was actually measured on. Attempt 3 kept the same sponsor and the same technical proposal, but raised that illustrative alignment to roughly 90% by connecting it to on-call sustainability, a metric the manager's own manager was tracking. These percentages are teaching numbers, not a real prediction formula. Drag the framing-alignment slider to see how adoption likelihood moves, holding the sponsor's own capacity to act fixed.
items.compute: const power = params.sponsorPower / 100; const alignment = params.framingAlignment / 100; const likelihood = Math.round(power * alignment * 100); return { likelihood };
